title: My brother and I didn't speak for three years
lesson: Being right is terrible company. If you stopped talking to someone over one sentence, call first; they are probably waiting too.

beats.vo: My little brother and I didn't say one word to each other for three years.
beats.shot: Bright low winter sunlight from the window, clear and white. The small kitchen of an old terraced house in a northern English seaside town: white walls, pale-blue painted wooden cupboards, a butcher-block worktop, a white ceramic sink under a sash window onto a small yard with a grey stone wall and a strip of grey-blue sea beyond the rooftops, an old cream gas cooker, a small square scrubbed-pine table with mismatched wooden chairs. A small white jug of pine sprigs on the windowsill, a bowl of clementines on the table, a grey wool throw over one chair. The narrow hallway of the old terraced house: a worn dark-red stair runner on a narrow staircase with white banisters, coat hooks on the wall, a dark-blue front door with a small square window and a brass letterbox. Ellie (long chestnut-brown hair in a loose low braid over her LEFT shoulder, light freckles across the nose and cheeks, light-hazel eyes), in an oatmeal-coloured cable-knit jumper, sits on the third stair of the narrow staircase holding a phone to her ear, seen from the side, eyes down, a calm still face, waiting. A calm relaxed face, mouth closed. Medium shot, faces at medium size.

beats.vo: So today I'm making banana bread. Extra walnuts. The way he's liked it since he was six.
beats.shot: Bright low winter sunlight from the window, clear and white. The small kitchen of an old terraced house in a northern English seaside town: white walls, pale-blue painted wooden cupboards, a butcher-block worktop, a white ceramic sink under a sash window onto a small yard with a grey stone wall and a strip of grey-blue sea beyond the rooftops, an old cream gas cooker, a small square scrubbed-pine table with mismatched wooden chairs. A small white jug of pine sprigs on the windowsill, a bowl of clementines on the table, a grey wool throw over one chair. Close-up over the worktop, top-down: a paper-lined loaf tin filled two-thirds with smooth pale-yellow raw banana batter; Ellie's hands (slender young fair hands, short natural pale-pink nails, no rings) in a cream chunky-knit cardigan sleeves scatter a handful of walnut halves over the batter, a few sinking in unevenly. Walnuts dropping softly onto batter. A completely still locked-off frame: the camera never moves, every edge of the window, cupboards and door frame stays in the same place from the first frame to the last.

beats.vo: And then there he was.
beats.still: Bright low winter sunlight from the window, clear and white. Outside the old terraced house: a dark-blue front door with a small square window and a brass letterbox, a worn stone step, a grey terraced street, bright cold winter sun. Seen from the pavement: Sam (short chestnut-brown hair a little wavy and messy on top, light freckles, light-hazel eyes, light reddish-brown stubble, a thin dark-brown leather cord bracelet on his LEFT wrist), in a navy-blue wool crew-neck jumper over a white T-shirt, with a dark charcoal wool coat open over it, stands on the worn stone step in front of the closed dark-blue front door, holding a sleeping newborn swaddled in a cream cable-knit blanket in the crook of his arm, looking at the door. A whole person. A calm relaxed face, mouth closed. Medium shot, faces at medium size.
